events.subtitle: JUJU JAZZ LIVE 2026 — EVERYTHING IS DELICIOUS IN AUTUMN!!
events.category: Japan / Vocal jazz / Annual Blue Note Tokyo series
events.factual_description: Blue Note Tokyo presents JUJU JAZZ LIVE 2026: EVERYTHING IS DELICIOUS IN AUTUMN!! on November 12, 13, 14, 16, 17 and 18, 2026. November 12, 13, 16, 17 and 18 have sets beginning at 5:30 PM and 8:30 PM; November 14 has sets at 4:30 PM and 7:30 PM. The announced band is JUJU on vocals, Masato Ishinari on guitar, Shinichi Kusama on piano, SOKUSAI on bass, Masanori Amakura on drums, plus Shunichi Oshima on keyboards/saxophone November 12-13 and Masato Honma on keyboards/saxophone November 14 and 16-18. Sony Music's official announcement states that JUJU has held this Blue Note Tokyo jazz live series every year since 2011 and that 2026 is its 16th year. Blue Note Tokyo lists a music charge of ¥11,000 and a general/Jam Session lottery application window of September 25-28, 2026.

en.why_it_matters: This belongs on RADAR because it is a real Tokyo live-music practice, not a pop singer making a novelty jazz stop. JUJU has returned to Blue Note Tokyo for a jazz series every year since 2011, and the club-scale format puts a singer with deep New York roots in front of a compact working band rather than the production architecture of a hall or arena tour. The value is continuity: standards, jazz phrasing and band interaction have become a parallel strand of her career that lives specifically in this room-sized setting.
en.trip_verdict: Keep it on the board if November in Tokyo overlaps the six-night run, especially if the itinerary has room for vocal jazz or for a distinctly Japanese bridge between mainstream pop and club jazz. Twelve sets create plenty of flexibility, so I would fit one around scarcer masters, premieres or one-night encounters rather than moving those to make room.

es.why_it_matters: Entra al RADAR porque esto ya es una práctica real de la vida musical de Tokio, no una cantante pop haciendo una excursión de jazz por novedad. JUJU vuelve a Blue Note Tokyo con una serie jazzística todos los años desde 2011, y la escala de club pone a una cantante con raíces musicales profundas en Nueva York frente a una banda compacta de trabajo, lejos de la arquitectura de producción de una gira de arena o de hall. El valor está en la continuidad: standards, fraseo jazzístico e interacción de banda se volvieron una línea paralela de su carrera que vive especialmente bien a esta escala.
es.trip_verdict: La tendría en el tablero si noviembre en Tokio coincide con estas seis noches, sobre todo si el itinerario tiene espacio para jazz vocal o para ese puente muy japonés entre pop masivo y jazz de club. Doce sets dan muchísimo margen, así que acomodaría uno alrededor de maestros más escasos, estrenos o encuentros de una sola noche en vez de desplazar éstos.
